name: Minsa

anatomy.part: apex of the kite, top point where the tail ribbon is knotted
right corner of the kite, on the crossbar
bottom point of the kite, where the long string is tied on
left corner of the kite, the bright bridle knot on the crossbar
far end of the tail ribbon, trailing out to the left
long string, the elbow where it turns down
long string, far down over the water
loose end of the string, left long for the child to follow

myth: Every spring the old women fly a kite with its string left long, for a child who went under. Once there was a girl named Minsa who had no one left to fly with, so she flew her own kite and let the string run out over the water. Tavo the Gale saw it and laughed, but he could not cut the string. Ennu the Kite-Wright had stitched that kite from her father's old sail, and the sail held. Mother Hesk, who winds every string and keeps count, marked the length of it and said nothing. Sil, who still searches the sea for Aun, came down the Lamp Road to look. She saw how far the string went, and said a long string is a road, and roads are for coming home by. So the kite stays up, its string hanging into the dark water, and the grandmothers say that if the wind is kind, somebody will come up it.
verse:
Long string to the sea
the child's kite hangs on its line
come up, the wind's kind
